(This evening through Monday)...
Issued at 243 PM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

Surface analysis early afternoon shows a cold front well east of 
Indiana, along the east coast. A very large and strong area of high 
pressure was found over Dakotas, spreading its influence well east, 
across the Great Lakes, Indiana and the Ohio Valley in the wake of 
the front. Water vapor this afternoon shows a deep trough in place 
over Ontario with nearly zonal flow in place across Illinois and 
Indiana near the base of the trough. Ridging was found exiting the 
Rockies, with a subsequent trough over the intermountain west in 
tow. Cool and dry NW flow was in place across Indiana as the large 
high approached from the west. GOES19 shows abundant lake cloud over 
northern Indiana drifting southeast.

Tonight and Tuesday...

Dry and cool weather will be expected tonight through Tuesday night. 
The strong high pressure system over the Dakotas will be the 
dominate feature as it pushes to MN and IA late tonight before 
reaching the Great Lakes on Tuesday night. The high will be the 
result of ongoing subsidence due to ridging building aloft and 
passing through the upper midwest. Forecast soundings continue to 
show a dry column tonight, but some upper level saturation is 
suggested to begin to arrive late Tuesday and and Tuesday Night. 

Ongoing cold air advection is in play today with 850mb temps 
remaining around -4C. This will result in lows in the middle 20s, 
with upper 20s in urban areas, under mostly clear skies.

Highs on Tuesday should be slightly warmer than persistence as the 
cooler airmass modifies somewhat. Highs should reach the lower to 
middle 40s.

Wednesday...

Changeable weather is expected on Wednesday. A significant upper 
trough with developing dual upper lows is expected to push out of 
the Rockies reaching the plains states on Wednesday. This is a 
powerful trough with impressive dynamics. Southerly flow aloft is 
expected to begin aloft and slowly decent through the column over 
the course of the day. Within the lower levels the previous high 
pressure system will be found well to the northeast, but keep a cool 
and dry northeasterly flow in place at the surface. This will set up 
an overruning situation as and models show a surge of warm gulf 
moisture streaming north toward Indiana through the day. By 
afternoon, forecast soundings show deep saturation within the column 
with pwats near 0.75 inches. Surface level organization does not 
appear as robust. Wednesday will begin with an inverted trough 
stretching from the Gulf across MS and western TN, aiding in 
overruning, but across Indiana these features are not nearly as 
pronounced. The 295K isentropic surface shows moderate upglide by 
late afternoon with specific humidities over 4 g/kg.  Strong 
cyclogenesis is expected to develop east of FL on Wednesday Night. 
This will help develop strong cyclonic flow across the eastern third 
of the country including Indiana. This should enhance the total 
setup across Central Indiana by Wednesday night, allowing for more 
numerous and increasing rain showers across the area. Confidence for 
rain on Wednesday night into Thursday is high.

Thursday and Thursday night...

The ptype forecast is extremely tricky during this forecast period 
owing to temperatures being very close to critical thresholds for 
rain or snow along with very subtle placement discrepancies of 
stronger upper level dynamic cooling. Model consensus is that a 
strengthening upper low will be centered near the MS valley at 12Z 
Thursday. The GFS has the furthest north position near STL while the 
Operational Euro is showing the furthest south position near the 
Bootheel of MO. Although these differences would be considered 
normal for a 3 day forecast, the thermodynamic consequences to these 
differences are noteworthy. The further north position of the GFS 
favors a colder solution with areas of central Indiana receiving 
warning level snowfall (6-8 inches), while the Euro on the other end 
of the spectrum has a thermal profile supporting all rain (albeit a 
cold rain) with temps staying above 32F the entire period. The rest 
of the medium range guidance falls in between these two "outliers". 
The Operational Euro did a superior job forecasting the phasing 
troughs/snow potential 7 days out, which makes it more interesting 
that its now the warmest solution. Despite this, confidence is 
increasing in sufficient dynamic cooling to swing closer to the GFS 
solution with a few inches of wet snow possible in narrow band/s 
near the primary deformation zone, although this location is too 
difficult to narrow down 3 days out. The NBM being a blend of multi 
models/ensembles will continue to show a rain/snow mix for Thursday 
night, but would expect the snow will mix in Thursday afternoon if a 
faster/colder solutions such as the RRFS and GFS verify.  Whatever 
model verifies on the ptype, there is excellent agreement that
